title: arxiv_2511.06175v1
universal_lens: Constraint satisfaction with information-theoretic weighting enables probabilistic role inference in social deduction games via hard/soft logical partitions. Constraint satisfaction formalism unifies game state updates via logical assertions and probabilistic hypotheses.
gsi_mapping: Bayesian posterior over role assignments updated via CSP constraints; conformal prediction ensures calibrated uncertainty estimates for belief states. Bayesian inference engine maps constraint sets to posterior belief distributions over role assignments using CSP-derived likelihoods.
gse_mapping: Situationally grounded state transitions driven by evidence and hypothesis constraints; dynamic role belief updates enable real-time tactical reasoning. Situational reasoning module encodes game dynamics through state transitions governed by event-triggered constraints and agent-specific views.

primitives.name: Role Constraint Partition
primitives.verbatim_quote: We introduce CSP4SDG, a probabilistic, constraint–satisfaction framework that analyses gameplay objectively.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'R': 'set of possible roles', 'C': 'constraint set', 'P(R|C)': 'posterior probability distribution over roles given constraints'}
primitives.assumptions: Gameplay data can be abstracted into discrete constraints; roles are mutually exclusive and collectively exhaustive.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When constraint set C becomes inconsistent, P(R|C) collapses to zero probability for all role assignments.

layer2.mapping: Each role assignment maps to a node in a Bayesian network where edges represent logical dependencies derived from CSP constraints.
layer2.telemetry: Posterior entropy reduction across role assignments during gameplay evolution.

primitives.name: Constraint Type Classification
primitives.verbatim_quote: Game events and dialogue are mapped to four linguistically-agnostic constraint classes—evidence, phenomena, assertions, and hypotheses.
primitives.assumptions: All game inputs can be parsed into one of four constraint types without loss of semantic fidelity.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When input cannot be classified into E/P/A/H, classification ambiguity increases entropy in the system.

layer2.mapping: Each constraint type defines a kernel function in a probabilistic space that determines how much influence it has on role assignment likelihood.
layer2.telemetry: Weighted contribution of each constraint class to final role posterior distribution.

primitives.name: Information Gain Scoring
primitives.verbatim_quote: Hard constraints prune impossible role assignments, while weighted soft constraints score the remainder; informationgain weighting links each hypothesis to its expected value under entropy reduction, and a simple closed-form scoring rule guarantees that truthful assertions converge to classical hard logic with minimum error.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'\\mathcal{I}(H)': 'information gain from hypothesis H', 'p(h_i)': 'prior probability of hypothesis h_i', 'p(h_i | D)': 'posterior probability after observing data D'}
primitives.assumptions: Entropy reduction due to new data leads to deterministic convergence of assertions to hard constraints.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When information gain approaches zero, further observations yield minimal change in role probabilities.

layer2.mapping: Information gain corresponds to mutual information between observed actions and inferred roles, enabling optimal query selection in active inference protocols.
layer2.telemetry: Expected reduction in entropy per hypothesis update during gameplay.

primitives.name: Real-Time Posterior Update
primitives.verbatim_quote: The resulting posterior over roles is fully interpretable and updates in real time.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'t': 'time step', 'P(R_t | D_{1:t})': 'posterior at time t conditioned on history up to t'}
primitives.assumptions: Observations arrive sequentially and are processed incrementally without recomputation of prior posteriors.
primitives.breakdown_regime: If observation stream contains contradictory evidence, posterior may oscillate or diverge unless corrected by soft constraint reweighting.

layer2.mapping: Each new observation modifies the kernel density estimate of the posterior distribution over roles using incremental Bayesian updating rules.
layer2.telemetry: Rate of change in posterior mean and variance per turn in simulated game environments.

primitives.name: Role Assertion Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: Assertions multiply S by a large factor wA ≫1, whereas hypotheses add small weights wlow, wmid and whigh(dataset-specific, all less than 1).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'S(a)': 'Score function of assignment a, dimensionless', 'w_A': 'Large assertion weight, w_A \\gg 1, dimensionless', 'r': 'Role type, e.g., Percival, Merlin, etc., categorical', 's': 'Speaker player index, integer'}
primitives.assumptions: Role claims are either true or false; assertion increases score proportionally to confidence.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When speaker role matches claimed identity, score amplifies exponentially.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI's belief update mechanism where assertions act as evidence multipliers in Bayesian networks.
layer2.telemetry: Accuracy of role identification under truthful assertions.

primitives.name: Evil Status Hypothesis
primitives.verbatim_quote: Constraint Format shows the abstract grammar used by the extractor; Mathematical Representation shows how each constraint modifies the score S(a) of an assignment a.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'S(a)': 'Score function of assignment a, dimensionless', 'w_{\\text{mid}}': 'Medium hypothesis weight, 0 < w_{\\text{mid}} < 1, dimensionless', 't': 'Target player index, integer', 'evil(t)': 'Boolean indicating if t is evil, binary'}
primitives.assumptions: Weak suspicion implies low-confidence inference about target's alignment.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Score increment when player is suspected evil but not confirmed.

layer2.mapping: Used in GSE to model uncertainty propagation during voting rounds.
layer2.telemetry: False positive rate in identifying evil players based on vote patterns.

primitives.name: Constraint Satisfaction Solver Interface
primitives.verbatim_quote: We then feed the resulting constraint sets sequence directly to the CSP solver.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'\\mathcal{C}': 'Set of constraints, finite collection of predicates', 'c_i': 'Individual constraint, logical formula', '\\mathcal{F}': 'Constraint grammar mapping events to logical forms'}
primitives.assumptions: All constraints are consistent within a valid game state.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Solver fails when inconsistent constraints are introduced.

layer2.mapping: Directly interfaces with GSE's core logic engine for real-time decision-making.
layer2.telemetry: Number of valid solutions returned per game state.

primitives.name: Perspective-Based Scoring Function
primitives.verbatim_quote: We evaluate three perspectives: the objective view (public evidence only), each good role's private view (Merlin, Percival, Servant, Bystander), and each evil role's view (Assassin, Mafia).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'S^{\\text{view}}(a)': 'Scoring function under specific role perspective, dimensionless', 'w_i': 'Weight associated with event i, scalar', '\\text{event}_i': 'Observable event relevant to view, boolean'}
primitives.assumptions: Each role has unique information access affecting scoring.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Scoring diverges between roles due to asymmetric knowledge.

layer2.mapping: Enables GSE to simulate multiple agent viewpoints in adversarial environments.
layer2.telemetry: Difference in accuracy between objective and private views.

primitives.name: Assertion-Guided Constraint Satisfaction
primitives.verbatim_quote: Bakhtin, A.; Brown, N.; Dinan, E.; Farina, G.; Flaherty, C.; Fried, D.; Goff, A.; Gray, J.; Hu, H.; Jacob, A.; et al.
primitives.assumptions: Markov chain Monte Carlo ergodicity, Metropolis-Hastings acceptance criteria, adaptive proposal tuning via gradient estimation.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Non-negligible rejection rates when posterior geometry is highly correlated or multimodal.

layer2.mapping: Bayesian posterior inference over hidden player roles, where constraints encode logical consistency between actions and role-specific behavior. Telemetry: posterior variance reduction.
layer2.telemetry: Posterior variance reduction, constraint satisfaction rate

primitives.name: Role-Classification via Lexical Pragmatics
primitives.verbatim_quote: Mafia: A Theoretical Study of Players and Coalitions in a Partial Information Environment.
primitives.assumptions: Lexical markers (e.g., politeness, reciprocity) are conditionally independent given hidden role, and training data matches test distribution.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Performance degradation when deceptive players exploit linguistic patterns differently than observed during training.

layer2.mapping: Discriminative classification of hidden states using observable action sequences, analogous to state estimation in partially observable Markov decision processes (POMDPs). Telemetry: classification accuracy on held-out role assignments.

primitives.name: Commitment Strategies for Coalition Formation
primitives.verbatim_quote: Keeping the story straight: A comparison of commitment strategies for a social deduction game.
primitives.assumptions: Coalition members share a common utility function, and commitment mechanisms are immune to external manipulation or coercion.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Collusion failure when internal incentives diverge from collective objectives, leading to defection.

layer2.mapping: Mechanism design for stable coalition structures in non-cooperative games, leveraging side-payments or reputation systems to enforce binding agreements. Telemetry: coalition stability metrics.
layer2.telemetry: Coalition stability rate, average coalition size

primitives.name: Mixed Constraint Satisfaction Framework
primitives.verbatim_quote: Mixed constraint satisfaction: A framework for decision problems under incomplete knowledge.
primitives.assumptions: Constraint sets are satisfiable with some probability, and uncertainty is captured by a discrete probability mass function over possible constraint subsets.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Computational intractability when the number of possible constraint combinations grows exponentially with problem size.

layer2.mapping: Probabilistic satisfiability in adversarial environments, where constraints represent plausible actions conditioned on imperfect information. Telemetry: satisfiability probability estimates.

reasoning_traces.think: In Chapter 1, the core thesis revolves around the formalization of role identification within Social Deduction Games (SDGs) through a probabilistic constraint satisfaction framework named CSP4SDG. The method begins by parsing raw gameplay logs into four constraint types—evidence, phenomena, assertions, and hypotheses—each carrying distinct logical weightings. Evidence and phenomena act as hard constraints that eliminate impossible role assignments, while assertions and hypotheses serve as soft constraints with varying degrees of influence. This partitioning allows for a principled application of information theory to quantify how much new data reduces uncertainty about player roles. The framework employs a closed-form scoring mechanism that ensures truthful assertions converge toward classical hard logic, thereby minimizing error propagation. Real-time posterior updates are enabled through efficient constraint propagation algorithms, allowing the system to maintain an interpretable belief state. The integration of lightweight LLMs facilitates natural language processing without sacrificing scalability or interpretability. Empirical validation across multiple datasets demonstrates superior performance over pure LLM baselines, confirming that principled probabilistic reasoning offers a viable alternative or enhancement to neural architectures for SDG inference tasks.
